messages.subject: RE: About length_thresh
messages.body_plain:
Hi Tao,

The number of latent factors cannot exceed the number of normal samples if you use the normalize2() function. It’s similar to the fact that the number of PCs cannot exceed the matrix dimension in PCA.

Hope this clarifies,

Yuchao

messages.subject: RE: CODEX for Indentification of Somatic CNVs
messages.subject_clean: CODEX for Indentification of Somatic CNVs
messages.body_plain:
Hi Haiying,

Thanks for your interest in CODEX! CODEX adopts a cross-sample normalization to estimate exon-wise and sample-wise latent factors, GC content bias, exon-specific bias etc. With this said, it doesn’t directly compare a tumor normal versus its normal control. Therefore, the CNV output has each row as a CNV event for a specific sample. For the normal samples, they will be the germline CNVs, for the tumor samples, they may be somatic or germline CNVs and thus need to be compared against the normal calls. I suggest you load your results onto IGV for visualization.

Hope that this clarifies, please let me know if you have any further questions with regard to the software. I am cc’ing our users’ mailing list in case others have similar questions.

Cheers,

Yuchao

From: Kong, Haiying [mailto:h.k...@dkfz-heidelberg.de]
Sent: Tuesday, June 14, 2016 11:32 AM
To: Jiang, Yuchao <yuc...@wharton.upenn.edu>
Subject: CODEX for Indentification of Somatic CNVs

Dear Dr. Jiang,

  We are trying to use CODEX package to identify somatic CNVs for our whole exome sequence data from paired samples of blood and tumor.

  Each patient provides paired sample of blood and tumor, and these are whole exome sequenced.

  The code I am running for one chromosome is:

  # bambed:

  bambedObj = getbambed(bamdir = bamdir,

                        bedFile = bedFile,

                        sampname = sampname,

                        projectname = "PrimaryMelanoma1",

                        chr = chr)

  ##################################################################################################################

  # Coverage:

  coverageObj = getcoverage(bambedObj, mapqthres=20)

  ##################################################################################################################

  # GC content:

  gc = getgc(chr, bambedObj$ref)

  mapp = getmapp(chr, bambedObj$ref)

  ##################################################################################################################

  # QC filtering:

  qcObj = qc(coverageObj$Y, bambedObj$sampname, chr, bambedObj$ref, mapp, gc,

             cov_thresh=c(20,4000), length_thresh=c(20,2000), mapp_thresh=0.9, gc_thresh=c(10, 90))

  ##################################################################################################################

  # Normalization:

  normal = read.table("SampleInfo/Blood_Nevus.txt", header=FALSE, stringsAsFactors=FALSE, sep="\t")[ ,1]

  normObj = normalize2(qcObj$Y_qc, qcObj$gc_qc, K=1:max.k, normal_index=which(qcObj$sampname_qc %in% normal))

  ##################################################################################################################

  # Decide number of latent factors:

  choiceofK(normObj$AIC, normObj$BIC, normObj$RSS, normObj$K,

            filename=paste("Lock/CNV/CODEX/ChoiceK/chr", chr, ".pdf", sep=""))

  ##################################################################################################################

  # Determine CNVs:

  optK = normObj$K[which.max(normObj$BIC)]

  finalcall = segment(qcObj$Y_qc, normObj$Yhat, optK=optK, K=normObj$K, qcObj$sampname_qc, qcObj$ref_qc, bambedObj$chr,

                      lmax=200, mode="fraction")

  write.table(finalcall,

              paste("Lock/CNV/CODEX/ByChrom/chr", chr, "_K", optK, "_frac.txt", sep=""),

              row.names=FALSE, col.names=TRUE, quote=FALSE, sep="\t")

  save.image(file=paste("Lock/CNV/CODEX/ByChrom/chr", chr, "_K", optK, "_image.rda", sep=""),

             compress="xz")

  And the results I got has the form of:

sample_name     chr     cnv     st_bp   ed_bp   length_kb       st_exon ed_exon raw_cov norm_cov        copy_no lratio  mBIC    pvalue

B62047  22      dup    .........

B62047  22      del     .................

B64433  22      dup   ……………………..

T011    22      del      .....................

  I am expecting that one row is for one patient, that means that one row has 2 sample names, the paired samples from blood and tumor of one patient. But the result is showing one sample in one row.

  Could you please tell me how to interpret the results?

  Thank you so much.

  Best regards,

  Haiying
